subject.title: fix(sessions): keep dirty transcript search from blocking the gateway

question: Does the database-owned claim generation, mutation invalidation, final revision fence, and two-phase watchdog lifecycle provide the session-state guarantees maintainers want for dirty transcript reconciliation?
rationale: The implementation appears coherent and well proven, but it introduces a new asynchronous state machine whose failure modes can affect both persisted search correctness and Gateway availability; tests cannot substitute for owner acceptance of that lifecycle contract.

options.title: Approve the lifecycle
options.body: Confirm the state-machine contract and merge after exact-head checks and mergeability are green.

options.title: Require additional exact-head proof
options.body: Ask for a live concurrent-mutation run on the current head before accepting the claim and invalidation semantics.

options.title: Pause the worker design
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it if maintainers prefer a different reconciliation owner or architecture despite the demonstrated event-loop problem.

recommendation.title: Approve the lifecycle
recommendation.body: Confirm the state-machine contract and merge after exact-head checks and mergeability are green.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans core session persistence and Gateway availability rather than a narrow file-level repair.
